article_title: Development of the Feedback Quality Instrument: a guide for health professional educators in fostering learner-centred discussions.
citation: Johnson Christina E., Keating Jennifer L., Leech Michelle, Congdon Peter, Kent Fiona, Farlie Melanie K., Molloy Elizabeth K. (2021). Development of the Feedback Quality Instrument: a guide for health professional educators in fostering learner-centred discussions. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-021-02722-8
title: The FQI five-domain framework for learner-centred feedback
description: The FQI framework organises educator feedback practice into five domains underpinned by a social constructivist perspective in which educators and learners co-create insights through interactive dialogue. The article states the FQI "contains five domains, three that occur somewhat sequentially, set the scene, analyse performance, plan improvement, and two that continue throughout the interaction, foster psychological safety and foster learner agency". Items describe observable educator behaviours intended to engage learners in an interactive learning dialogue rather than one-way tips.
requirements: Items must describe observable educator behaviours that are generally applicable to verbal face-to-face feedback interactions, target a single distinct attribute, and be unambiguous
constraints: The FQI was designed in one country and tested within one major healthcare network, so applicability to other countries and contexts is unknown, per the authors
target_learners: health professional students and clinicians in workplace clinical settings
examples: Raters used the provisional instrument to rate educator behaviours in 36 authentic feedback videos on a 0-2 consistency scale
